name: SOC 2 Type II
description: SOC 2 Type II overlay — Trust Services Criteria for service organizations. Universal enterprise compliance baseline. Activated by general business data or personal information declarations. Every agent startup selling to enterprises needs SOC 2.

evidence_requirements: Information security policy communicated to personnel and third parties (CC1.1)
Board or management oversight of internal controls demonstrated (CC1.2)
Organizational structure with defined reporting lines and authorities (CC1.2)
Responsibility for internal controls assigned and communicated (CC1.3)
Risk assessment process identifies and analyzes risks to service commitments (CC3.1)
Risk mitigation activities defined and monitored (CC3.2)
Management monitors internal controls effectiveness on an ongoing basis (CC4.1)
Deficiencies communicated and corrective actions taken (CC4.2)
Information assets inventoried and classified (CC6.1)
Asset management policies cover full lifecycle from acquisition to disposal
Software and infrastructure inventories maintained (CC6.6)
Authorized components tracked with version and configuration state
Data classified based on sensitivity and regulatory requirements (CC6.1)
Classification scheme applied consistently across systems
Vendor risk assessment and due diligence processes documented (CC9.2)
Third-party service provider controls evaluated and monitored (CC9.2)
Risk assessment identifies threats and vulnerabilities relevant to service commitments (CC3.2)
Risk tolerance defined by management and documented
Logical access security controls restrict access to authorized users (CC6.1)
Authentication mechanisms appropriate to the sensitivity of data and systems (CC6.1)
Evidence of continuous operation of access controls over Type II audit period
Least privilege access implemented and enforced (CC6.3)
Access provisioning and de-provisioning procedures documented and followed (CC6.2)
Periodic access reviews conducted and documented (CC6.3)
Change management process implemented for system components (CC8.1)
Changes tested and approved before deployment to production
Data transmission restricted to authorized channels (CC6.7)
Confidential information protected during transmission and storage (C1.1)
Processing integrity validated for system outputs (PI1.1)
System activity logged and monitored for security events (CC7.1, CC7.2)
Logs include sufficient detail for incident investigation
Log retention meets contractual and regulatory obligations
Configuration management procedures documented and followed (CC8.1)
Baseline configurations established and deviations detected
Encryption used for data in transit and at rest per policy (CC6.7)
Cryptographic controls appropriate to data classification
Input validation and error handling implemented (CC7.1)
Systems protected against unauthorized modification
Security event monitoring and anomaly detection active (CC7.2)
Events analyzed and triaged based on severity (CC7.3)
Evidence of continuous monitoring operation over Type II audit period
Configuration monitoring detects unauthorized changes (CC7.1)
Monitoring covers system components relevant to service commitments
Internal control effectiveness evaluated on an ongoing basis (CC4.1)
Deficiencies identified and communicated to management
Security event monitoring includes log integrity validation (CC7.3)
Tamper detection mechanisms in place for audit records
Incident response procedures defined, communicated, and tested (CC7.3, CC7.4)
Incidents identified, reported, and resolved in a timely manner
Escalation procedures defined for security incidents (CC7.4)
Communication protocols for internal and external stakeholders documented
Incident investigation procedures include evidence preservation (CC7.5)
Evidence retained per contractual and regulatory requirements
System recovery and business continuity plans documented and tested (A1.2)
Recovery time and recovery point objectives defined and achievable
Post-incident reviews conducted with lessons learned documented (CC4.2)
Corrective actions tracked to implementation

reporting_obligations.assessment_type: SOC 2 Type I (point-in-time design effectiveness) or Type II (operating effectiveness over 6-12 months). Audit performed by licensed CPA firm. Report is restricted-use — NDA typically required to share.
reporting_obligations.reporting_entity: Licensed CPA firm (AICPA-accredited). Report distributed to user entities and their auditors under NDA.

human_oversight_mandates.description: SOC 2 does not explicitly mandate human oversight of AI systems, but CC4.1 requires ongoing monitoring of internal controls and CC1.4 requires management oversight of the control environment.

notes: SOC 2 Type II is the universal B2B compliance baseline. Covers all five Trust Services Categories: Security (CC), Availability (A), Processing Integrity (PI), Confidentiality (C), and Privacy (P). All controls at standard threshold — SOC 2 focuses on demonstrating controls are designed AND operating effectively over a period, not specific technical thresholds. When DC-PII is active, Privacy criteria (P1) also apply.
